why: The evidence behind ADR-0142's desktop declaration: the amendment left mac-safari's 16/16 inert rotation zeros 'for the desktop runner to declare on its own evidence'. These three sweeps are that evidence — the same rotation cells (--actions=rotation, campaign landscape viewport 1366x915, 9 repeats = 8 scored samples per rotation label, 32 per engine) driven through the desktop Playwright transport on each engine, deciding per engine whether post-resize first frames are structurally zero (the Safari engine shape) or carry dynamic range (the gated shape).
capturedFrom: perf:web:actions --actions=rotation --repeats=9 --viewport=1366x915 --report-only, local Mac (macOS darwin), quiet host, production preview build at the stack's fork point c12c46cd662a9b1cbf237a2ff09c4f394b93fb14

kept.note: 31 of 32 scored rotation first frames read exactly 0.0 ms; the single non-zero sample is 6.0 ms, sub-frame and not app-attributable. WebKit dispatches resize inside the rendering turn whose rAF timestamp the probe records — the iPad Safari construction — so the gate cannot discriminate: declared N/A (ROTATION_INERT_DESKTOP_ENGINES).
0 of 32 scored rotation first frames read exactly zero; the distribution spreads 0.04-8.0 ms across every rotation label. Real post-resize dynamic range — the gate stays live for mac-chrome.
Bimodal: 11 of 32 scored rotation first frames land sub-1 ms, the rest 7.3-9.5 ms. The variation is real dynamic range, not a constructed zero — the gate stays live for mac-firefox.
